events.title: The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland is born
events.description: The Act of Union took effect at the start of the new century. It merged the Kingdom of Great Britain and the Kingdom of Ireland into a single state, governed from Westminster.
events.significance: The union lasted until 1922 and shaped British and Irish history through the 19th century. Its legacy is still debated in both countries.

events.title: The Emancipation Proclamation takes effect
events.description: President Abraham Lincoln's final proclamation took effect in the midst of the Civil War. It declared that enslaved people in the Confederate states were free. It also opened the way for Black men to serve in the Union forces.
events.significance: It changed the moral purpose of the war and set the United States on the path to abolishing slavery nationwide with the 13th Amendment.

events.title: Batista flees Cuba as the revolution triumphs
events.description: Dictator Fulgencio Batista left Cuba for the Dominican Republic as revolutionary forces closed in. Rebel fighters then took control of Havana, and Fidel Castro's movement took power.
events.significance: The revolution turned Cuba into a communist state allied with the Soviet Union. It became a central flashpoint of the Cold War.

events.title: Euro notes and coins enter everyday life
events.description: Twelve European Union countries put euro banknotes and coins into circulation. Millions of people swapped their national currencies for the new money.
events.significance: It was one of the largest currency changeovers in history. It created a shared currency used across much of Europe.
